examples.en: The two of them got married last spring.

examples.ko: 혼인하는 두 사람에게 축하 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: I congratulated the couple who were getting married.
To be legally married, you have to submit documents.
They got married and live in the countryside.

examples.ko: 스무 살에 혼인한 할머니가 옛날이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother, who married at twenty, told me old stories.
I have someone to marry, so I am preparing to move.

explain: 일상에서는 '결혼하다'를 훨씬 많이 말해요. '혼인하다'는 법, 서류, 옛날이야기처럼 격식 있는 글에서 자주 나와요. '혼인 신고'처럼 서류에 쓰는 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: We filed our marriage registration at the district office yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼인하다'와 잘 어울리는 서류 관련 표현이고, 법적으로 부부가 되는 절차를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document-related phrase that pairs well with '혼인하다'; it refers to the legal procedure of becoming a married couple.

phrases.example: 혼인한 지 오 년이 된 부부예요.
phrases.en: They are a couple who have been married for five years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼인하다'를 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 형태라서 글이나 서류에서 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of '혼인하다', which sounds natural in writing and formal documents.

phrases.en: The two of them are getting married next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서는 '혼인하다'보다 '결혼하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same thing, but '결혼하다' is much more common than '혼인하다' in everyday conversation.

explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say '결혼하다' far more often. 혼인하다 shows up in law, paperwork and old stories. It pairs well with official terms like '혼인 신고' (marriage registration).

t90.ax: The two of them got married last spring.

examples.ko: 서커스 단원이 공중에서 곡예를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The circus performer showed acrobatics in the air.
The children clapped in amazement at the acrobatics.
The motorcycle stunt show was really nerve-racking.

examples.ko: 곡예 운전을 하는 차 때문에 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by a car driving recklessly.

examples.ko: 곡예가 끝나자 관객들이 일어서서 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: When the acrobatics ended, the audience stood and applauded.

examples.ko: 곡예처럼 위험한 운전은 절대 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never drive dangerously like it's a stunt.

explain: 서커스처럼 몸으로 하는 아슬아슬한 재주를 말해요. 일상에서는 '곡예 운전'처럼 위험하게 움직일 때 비유로도 써요. 발음은 쓰인 대로가 아니라 [고계]예요.

phrases.example: 서커스 단원이 줄 위에서 곡예를 해요.
phrases.en: The circus performer does acrobatics on a rope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재주를 부린다는 뜻으로 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, meaning to perform acrobatic feats.

phrases.en: Stunt driving on a motorcycle is really dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 위험하게 모는 것을 비유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for driving in a risky way.

phrases.en: The acrobat did three spins in the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡예를 직업으로 하는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who performs acrobatics as a job.

explain_en: It refers to daring physical skills like those at a circus. In daily life it is also used figuratively for risky movement, as in '곡예 운전' (stunt-like driving). It is pronounced [고계], not as spelled.

examples.en: The idols' group dance was truly perfect.
Migratory birds perform a group dance in the sky.

examples.ko: 열 명이 함께 추는 군무가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The group dance performed by ten people was cool.

examples.ko: 군무 연습 때문에 매일 늦게까지 남아요.
examples.en: I stay late every day because of group dance practice.
In a ballet ensemble dance, the dancers have to be in sync.
This song is famous for its group choreography.

explain: 여러 사람이 함께 추는 춤을 말하고, 혼자 추는 '독무'의 반대예요. 아이돌 춤이 정확하게 맞으면 '칼군무'라고 많이 말해요. 새 떼나 물고기 떼가 한꺼번에 움직이는 모습을 '군무'에 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: That group is famous for its razor-sharp synchronized dancing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 정확하게 맞춰 추는 춤을 말하는 요즘 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modern term for group dancing performed in perfect sync.

phrases.example: 무대에서 열 명이 함께 군무를 춰요.
phrases.en: Ten people dance a group dance together on stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing with the verb 추다 (to dance).

phrases.en: The group dance scene in the movie was really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 공연에서 여럿이 춤추는 부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the part of a film or show where many people dance.

explain_en: It means a dance performed by many people together, the opposite of '독무' (a solo dance). When an idol group's moves match precisely, people often say '칼군무'. Flocks of birds or schools of fish moving together are also compared to a 군무.

examples.ko: 이 악보에는 도돌이표가 두 개 있어요.
examples.en: This sheet music has two repeat signs.

examples.ko: 도돌이표를 만나면 앞으로 돌아가서 다시 연주해요.
examples.en: When you meet a repeat sign, you go back and play again.

examples.ko: 선생님이 도돌이표 부분을 한 번 더 치라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told me to play the repeated section once more.

examples.ko: 도돌이표를 못 봐서 중간에 끝내 버렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't see the repeat sign and ended in the middle.
Every meeting is like a loop, and it's frustrating.
My days repeat the same, like a loop.

explain: 악보에서 앞부분으로 돌아가 다시 연주하라고 알려 주는 기호예요. 요즘은 같은 일이나 말이 끝없이 되풀이될 때 '도돌이표 같다'고도 해요.

phrases.en: Our conversations always go around in circles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 이야기나 상황이 끝없이 되풀이되어 답답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the same topic or situation repeats endlessly and feels frustrating.

explain_en: This is the sign in sheet music telling you to go back and play a section again. Today people also say '도돌이표 같다' when the same things or words repeat endlessly.

examples.en: A batter came up in the bottom of the ninth with the bases loaded.
A grand slam was hit, and the stadium got fired up.
The pitcher got through the bases-loaded jam well.
When the bases were loaded, the whole crowd stood up.

examples.ko: 저는 만루에서 삼진을 당하는 장면이 제일 아쉬워요.
examples.en: The most disappointing thing for me is a strikeout with the bases loaded.
The team lost after missing a bases-loaded chance.

explain: 야구에서 1루, 2루, 3루에 모두 주자가 있는 상황을 말해요. '만루 홈런', '만루 위기', '만루 찬스'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 자주 써요. 소리는 [말루]로 나요.

phrases.example: 만루 홈런 덕분에 우리 팀이 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Our team won thanks to the grand slam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주자가 모두 있을 때 친 홈런이라서 점수가 네 점 나요.
phrases.nuance_en: A home run hit with all bases loaded, worth four runs.

phrases.en: The pitcher got through the bases-loaded jam well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수비하는 팀 입장에서 위험한 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the fielding team's side for a dangerous situation.

phrases.en: A hit came with the bases loaded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공격하는 팀 입장에서 점수를 낼 좋은 기회를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the batting team's side for a great chance to score.

explain_en: In baseball, it means runners are on first, second and third base all at once. It is often placed before other words, as in '만루 홈런', '만루 위기' and '만루 찬스'. It is pronounced [말루].

examples.en: I play the bassoon in the orchestra.
The sound of the bassoon is low and soft.

examples.ko: 동생이 학교 밴드에서 바순을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is learning the bassoon in the school band.
In this piece, the bassoon carries the melody.
The bassoon is much bigger than the clarinet.
I want to become a bassoonist.

explain: 낮고 부드러운 소리를 내는 목관악기예요. '바순을 불다' 또는 '바순을 연주하다'라고 말해요. 오케스트라나 관악 합주에서 낮은 음을 맡을 때가 많아요.

phrases.en: I play the bassoon in the school band.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입으로 부는 악기라서 '불다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it's a wind instrument, '불다' (to blow) is used.

phrases.en: I learned the bassoon in college.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 공부하거나 배운다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about studying or learning the instrument.

phrases.en: The bassoonist came out onto the stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바순을 연주하는 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who plays the bassoon.

explain_en: It is a woodwind instrument with a low, soft sound. You say '바순을 불다' or '바순을 연주하다'. In orchestras and wind ensembles it often covers the low parts.

examples.en: He sang a serenade beneath her window.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 모차르트의 세레나데 중에서 가장 유명해요.
examples.en: This piece is the most famous of Mozart's serenades.
A serenade concert is held in the park in the evening.
I prepared a serenade for my love confession.

examples.ko: 세레나데는 밤에 연인에게 불러 주는 노래예요.
examples.en: A serenade is a song you sing to your lover at night.

examples.ko: 기타 반주에 맞춰 세레나데를 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm practicing a serenade to a guitar accompaniment.

explain: 밤에 연인에게 불러 주는 노래를 뜻하기도 하고, 클래식에서는 '소야곡'이라고도 하는 곡 종류를 가리켜요. 일상 대화보다는 음악 이야기나 낭만적인 장면에서 주로 써요.

phrases.example: 남자가 여자 친구에게 세레나데를 불러 줬어요.
phrases.en: The man sang a serenade for his girlfriend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연인에게 노래로 마음을 전하는 장면에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in scenes where someone sings their feelings to a lover.

phrases.en: The orchestra played a serenade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악 곡을 말할 때는 '연주하다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For the musical piece, it pairs with 연주하다 (to play).

phrases.en: This piece is a serenade that suits the night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 한자어로, 음악 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word with the same meaning, used in talk about music.

explain_en: It can mean a song sung to a lover at night, and in classical music it is a type of piece also called '소야곡'. You hear it more in talk about music or romantic scenes than in everyday conversation.

examples.ko: 밤새 광풍이 불어서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A violent wind blew all night, so I couldn't sleep.
The roof was blown away by the fierce wind.
The boats came back to port to avoid the storm winds.
The fierce wind didn't die down until dawn.

examples.ko: 부동산 광풍 속에서 집값이 크게 올랐어요.
examples.en: Housing prices rose sharply amid the property frenzy.
That song swept across the country like a storm.

explain: 몹시 사납게 부는 바람이에요. 일상에서 바람이 센 날은 '강풍'이나 '바람이 세다'라고 하고, '광풍'은 더 거칠고 글 같은 느낌이에요. 뉴스에서는 '투자 광풍'처럼 사회가 한쪽으로 휩쓸리는 모습을 비유할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: A raging wind blew all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 거세게 계속 불어닥친다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of a fierce wind that keeps battering.

phrases.example: 오늘은 강풍 때문에 비행기가 늦게 떠요.
phrases.en: Because of strong winds, the flight leaves late today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기예보나 일상에서는 '광풍'보다 '강풍'을 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In weather reports and daily talk, 'gangpung' sounds more natural than 'gwangpung'.

phrases.example: 몇 년 전에 코인 투자 광풍이 불었어요.
phrases.en: A cryptocurrency investment frenzy swept through a few years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회가 한쪽으로 휩쓸리는 현상을 바람에 빗대어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compares a society-wide rush in one direction to a wild wind.

explain_en: It means a wind that blows extremely fiercely. In daily life people say '강풍' or '바람이 세다' for a windy day, while '광풍' sounds rougher and more literary. In the news it is also used figuratively, as in '투자 광풍' (investment frenzy), when society gets swept in one direction.

examples.en: A thunderous noise came as the plane passed.
I suddenly heard a deafening noise and looked out the window.
A motorcycle roared down the alley.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 굉음이 계속 나서 너무 시끄러워요.
examples.en: Loud booming noises keep coming from the construction site, so it's very noisy.
The thunder rumbled like a roar and the child cried.
The train entered the tunnel with a roar.

explain: 그냥 큰 소리가 아니라 기계, 폭발, 천둥처럼 크게 울리는 소리에 어울려요. '굉음이 나다', '굉음을 내다', '굉음이 울리다'로 자주 말해요. 사람 목소리에는 보통 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: A motorcycle passed by with a roar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 차가 크게 울리는 소리를 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a machine or vehicle makes a booming sound.

phrases.en: A roar echoed from the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 소리가 멀리까지 울릴 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a loud sound that echoes far.

phrases.en: I was startled by the tremendous roar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 얼마나 큰지 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress how loud the sound is.

explain_en: It is not just any loud sound but a booming, resonant one like machines, explosions or thunder. Common patterns are '굉음이 나다', '굉음을 내다' and '굉음이 울리다'. It is not normally used for a person's voice.

examples.en: A sparrow walks along, wagging its tail.
A peacock's tail is truly magnificent.

examples.ko: 그 새는 꽁지에 하얀 털이 있어요.
examples.en: That bird has white feathers on its tail.
The chicken hid in the grass with only its tail showing.

examples.ko: 새가 꽁지로 균형을 잡으며 나뭇가지에 앉았어요.
examples.en: The bird landed on the branch, balancing with its tail.
I saw a long-tailed bird in the park.

explain: 새의 꼬리 쪽 깃털을 말해요. 강아지나 고양이 같은 동물에게는 '꼬리'를 써요.

phrases.example: 저 새는 꽁지가 길어서 눈에 잘 띄어요.
phrases.en: That bird has a long tail, so it stands out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새의 생김새를 말할 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for describing a bird's looks.

phrases.en: The peacock spread its tail wide.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새가 꼬리깃을 펼치는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a bird fanning out its tail feathers.

phrases.en: This bird's tail feathers are blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽁지'에 '깃(깃털)'이 붙어 꼬리 쪽 깃털만 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 깃 (feather) to 꽁지 refers specifically to the tail feathers.

explain_en: It refers to the tail feathers of a bird. For animals like dogs and cats, use '꼬리'.

examples.en: It's March, but it's still chilly because of the spring cold wind.
The chilly spring wind blew, so I took my scarf out again.
The cherry blossom petals are fluttering in the chilly spring wind.
The chilly flowering-season wind visits briefly in early spring.
I walked to school in the chilly spring wind.
Even in the chilly wind, the plum blossoms bloomed beautifully.

explain: 꽃이 필 무렵 이른 봄에 부는 쌀쌀한 바람이에요. 비슷한 시기의 추위를 가리키는 '꽃샘추위'와 함께 날씨 이야기에서 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The cherry blossoms bloomed late because of the cold snap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 아니라 이른 봄에 잠깐 다시 추워지는 날씨 전체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the whole late-winter cold spell, not just the wind.

phrases.en: A chilly spring wind is blowing, so my hands are cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불다'와 함께 써서 지금 바람이 분다고 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural with 불다 when saying the wind is blowing now.

phrases.en: I waited for the bus, shivering in the chilly wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 바람 때문에 춥다는 쓰임으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에, it shows being cold because of the wind.

explain_en: It is the chilly wind that blows in early spring around the time flowers bloom. You can hear it in weather talk along with '꽃샘추위', which refers to the cold of the same season.

examples.en: The waves roll in, swelling and falling.
The river flows with big, soft swells.
The barley field ripples in the wind.

examples.ko: 물이 넘실넘실 찬 컵을 조심히 옮겼어요.
examples.en: I carefully carried the cup, brimming with water.
A big ship drifts on the rolling sea.
In the autumn fields, the rice waves in great ripples.

explain: 물결이나 곡식이 크고 부드럽게 일렁이는 모양이에요. 뒤에 '흐르다, 흔들리다, 물결치다' 같은 동사가 잘 와요. '출렁출렁'보다 물이 가득 차서 크게 움직이는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The big river flows in rolling waves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 가득 차서 크게 흐르는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for water flowing broadly and fully.

phrases.en: The sea ripples in big, soft waves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물결이 부드럽고 크게 이는 모습을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes waves rising softly and widely.

phrases.en: The barley field ripples in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식이 바람에 물결처럼 흔들리는 모습에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for crops waving like water in the wind.

explain_en: It describes water or crops moving in big, soft swells. Verbs like '흐르다', '흔들리다' and '물결치다' often follow. Compared with '출렁출렁', it feels fuller, as if the water is brimming.

examples.ko: 올해 벚꽃 만개는 예상보다 일주일 빨라요.
examples.en: This year's cherry blossom full bloom is a week earlier than expected.

examples.ko: 꽃이 만개 직전이라 일주일 뒤에 가면 좋아요.
examples.en: The flowers are just before full bloom, so going in a week would be good.

examples.ko: 만개 시기에는 사람이 너무 많아서 걷기도 힘들어요.
examples.en: At peak bloom there are so many people that even walking is hard.

examples.ko: 남쪽에서 봄꽃의 만개 소식이 올라오고 있어요.
examples.en: News of spring flowers in full bloom is coming up from the south.

examples.ko: 매화의 만개를 기다리며 매일 공원에 가요.
examples.en: I go to the park every day waiting for the plum blossoms to be in full bloom.
We took a family photo in a rose garden in full bloom.

explain: 봄 날씨 뉴스에서 '개화'는 꽃이 피기 시작하는 때, 만개는 꽃이 활짝 핀 때라서 둘을 나눠서 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '활짝 피었어요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I checked the cherry blossom full-bloom time in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 활짝 피는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time when flowers are fully open.

phrases.en: The flowers are about to reach full bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 활짝 필 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when flowers are about to open fully.

phrases.en: Flowers have bloomed fully in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '만개'보다 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than '만개' in everyday conversation.

explain_en: In spring weather news, '개화' is when flowers begin to open and 만개 is when they are fully open, so the two are told apart. In everyday talk, '활짝 피었어요' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 봄이 되자 개울가 버들에 새잎이 났어요.
examples.en: When spring came, new leaves grew on the willows by the stream.
By the stream, the willow sways gently in the wind.

examples.ko: 연못 옆에 버들 한 그루가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A willow tree stands next to the pond.
The children made a whistle from willow branches.

examples.ko: 강가에 버들이 줄지어 서 있어서 풍경이 예뻐요.
examples.en: Willows stand in a row along the river, so the scenery is pretty.
A single willow leaf fell onto the water.

explain: 일상에서는 '버드나무'라고 말하는 경우가 많고, 버들은 시나 노래, '버들가지', '버들잎' 같은 말에서 자주 보여요. 가지가 길게 늘어진 나무는 '수양버들'이라고 해요. 부드럽고 가는 느낌을 줘서 글에서 풍경을 그릴 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: The willow branches sway gently in the spring breeze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버들의 가늘고 긴 가지를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the thin, long branches of a willow.

phrases.en: A willow leaf fell onto the pond.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버들의 잎을 가리킬 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that refers to willow leaves.

phrases.en: Weeping willows stand in a row along the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가지가 길게 늘어지는 버들의 종류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A kind of willow with long drooping branches.

explain_en: In daily life people often say '버드나무', while 버들 shows up in poems, songs and words like '버들가지' (willow branch) and '버들잎' (willow leaf). The kind with long hanging branches is called '수양버들' (weeping willow). It gives a soft, slender feel, so it suits descriptions of scenery in writing.
